title: interleaved-sso-claims-merge-causes-mixed-deny-and-admin-permission-states
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Several customers reported two related failures after a recent RBAC v2 rollout: (1) invited users intermittently receive PermissionDenied when accepting an SSO invite, and (2) concurrent long-lived sessions sometimes gain expanded admin privileges for a short window. Both symptoms trace to the new "delta-merge" logic that reconciles incoming SSO/SAML assertions with cached session claims and the audit index. Root cause: when multiple SSO assertions (e.g., group memberships + admin attribute) are processed concurrently for the same identity, the merge comparator can apply additive allow semantics to admin flags while a later deny (or TTL-expiry) is applied to group membership — producing a transient state where audit logs show mismatched before/after snapshots and the effective permission set is inconsistent across services.
reproduction_steps:
1) Test tenant with RBAC v2 enabled and session-cache TTL configured to 60s.
2) Create identity X with existing session (session A).
3) Trigger simultaneous SSO assertions: one from IdP1 that adds groups [team-alpha], another from IdP2 that sets admin=false and reduces group list.
4) Accept invite for new browser session B during overlap.
5) Observe: session B -> PermissionDenied for routes expecting team-alpha; session A -> temporarily has admin:true for ~10-30s before reconciliation.
6) Check audit index: two entries with non-monotonic diffs (audit shows admin added in later entry though group removed).
Expected: atomic, order-consistent reconciliation where denies and admin flags are resolved deterministically and audit captures consistent before/after snapshots.
impact_summary: Multiple mid-market customers (support tickets #CS-1682, #CS-1690) reported production outages for admin-only console routes and inability for new teammates to join projects. Estimated affected sessions: 120 sessions across 3 tenants in the last 48h. High business impact due to blocked admin workflows and confusion in audit trails for compliance teams.
root_cause_analysis: The delta-merge algorithm attempts conflict resolution by applying a three-phase merge: (1) union of allows, (2) subtract denies, (3) reconcile admin attribute by precedence. Under concurrent processing without strong ordering guarantees, phase (1) can observe an older assertion, then phase (3) from a different worker applies admin=true because it treats absence of deny as implicit allow. Additionally, audit snapshot generation occurs before final reconciliation, which causes logged snapshots to reflect intermediate states. Contributing factors: (a) session claim cache uses optimistic updates with compare-and-swap but lacks a global logical clock per-identity, (b) audit writer uses eventual consistency and is not transactional with claim updates.
proposed_fix:
1) Implement identity-scoped monotonic update token (logical clock) that increments on any incoming assertion; require merge to only apply assertions with higher token.
2) Change delta-merge to prioritize explicit deny attributes over additive allows when processing same logical clock.
3) Make audit snapshot generation transactional with claim store update (write-ahead commit): generate final before/after state after merge completes and include logical clock in audit entries.
4) Add regression tests simulating interleaved assertions and an e2e test that validates audit monotonicity.
Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-platform/pull/11827 (WIP)
mitigation_plan:
Short-term: added a guard that prevents admin attribute flips in-flight (feature flag: rbac.prevent-admin-flip). This reduces blast radius while we deploy the full fix. Notified customers and applied the flag to affected orgs.
Medium-term: deploy logical clock change to canary orgs and run synthetic tests.
Long-term: full rollout with migration script to backfill audit entries where possible.

qa_plan:
- Unit tests for merge precedence and logical clock increments.
- Integration tests running two IdP assertion streams against a single identity to assert deterministic final state.
- E2E test that asserts audit before/after snapshots are monotonic and include logical clock.
- Canary rollout with synthetic assertion flood; monitor "permission-anomalies" dashboard and customer feedback for 72h.
deployment_plan: 1) Merge PR behind feature flag. 2) Canary to canary-rbac-1 and canary-rbac-2 for 48-72h. 3) If stable, gradual rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% of orgs over 7 days. 4) Post-rollout audit reconciliation job run for orgs that experienced anomalies.
followups: Create migration job to backfill audit logical-clock field for last 7 days.
Policy: add automated synthetic test to CI that runs interleaved SSO assertions weekly.
